newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries sues Toyota over trade practices.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries sues Toyota over trade practices.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc. said on Tuesday it sued Toyota Motor Corp.'s U.S. sales arm in an Alabama state court, charging Toyota with unfair and deceptive trade practices.

A Republic spokesman said the company, controlled by billionaire H. Wayne Huizenga, claimed Toyota interfered illegally in its proposed acquisition of one Lexus and two Toyota dealerships from Dobbs Automotive Group in Alabama.
The suit was filed in the Circuit Court of Green County, Ala.

"Toyota has a series of internal policies that limit the number of dealerships any outside dealer can acquire to seven Toyota and three Lexus stores," the Republic spokesman said. "In addition, the policies hold that no single buyer can acquire more than one store every nine months.
"Basically, they have designed a little poison pill," the spokesman said, adding it would take a buyer five years to buy seven Toyota dealerships.

Republic also said Appleway Toyota of Spokane, Wash., filed a complaint with the Washington State Department of Motor Vehicles, charging that Toyota's policies interfere with the proposed sale of Appleway to Republic.
Republic said the Alabama suit seeks to prevent Toyota from using its policies to interfere with the proposed acquisition and the award of compensatory and punitive damages.
A Toyota Motor spokesman in New York confirmed Toyota's internal policies regarding the sale of dealerships.

"These policies exist so we can monitor the performance of the dealership for three quarters in order to see how well they are doing (under new management) before we approve the purchase," the spokesman said.
He added that the "policies have been in existence before Republic got into this business," about one-and-a-half years ago.

"Rebublic is in a big rush to buy up a lot of dealerships, and we want to see how well each dealership is doing under Rebublic management before they wind up controlling 20 percent of our sales," the spokesman said.
On Monday, Republic made its first major inroad into Europe's car rental market, agreeing to buy EuroDollar (Holdings) Plc for about 95.1 million pounds ($151 million).

Republic, headed by Blockbuster Video chain founder Huizenga, has also ploughed into the car rental industry in the past year, buying U.S. chains National Car Rental System and Alamo Rent-A-Car, which also has European operations.
